prediction:
#13, the wide-line CAP rule, with the half-pixel deadband the device forced.

WHAT THIS IS.  #13's extent phase landed exact and left ~908 px of
whole-capture coverage residual over the 48 non-void Line_* captures, 98.8% of
it within w/2 + 2 px of a vertex.  That class is the CAP.  The rule, derived
from the goldens with no fitted constant: the footprint never reaches past the
endpoints' own minor coordinates extended by w/2 -- the WIDTH, not the widened
extent E -- with both bounds rounded OUTWARD to whole pixel indices,

    minor index i is lit only if  floor(m_min - w/2) <= i <= ceil(m_max + w/2)

which turns the parallelogram into a hexagon where it bites.  On the ANALYTIC
MODEL (line_cap_phase.py --rivals, 48 captures, 1,967,133 golden ink px) it
scores 102 px against the unclipped footprint's 495, its nearest rival
floor + 1 scores 115, and the centre-sampled band 645.  On the shader's own
polygon rasterised at the device's 1/256 tie bias, 935 px -> 544.  The two are
DIFFERENT INSTRUMENTS and must not be quoted into one sentence.

WHY THIS REGISTRATION EXISTS: THE PREVIOUS ARM FAILED, AND IT WAS RIGHT TO.
The arm registered on a_ref 2e1c5790aa / b_ref 9fdc6b5d70 came back FAIL: 32
better, 10 worse, 124 same.  Eight of the ten worse were between w = 4 and
w = 14, where all three offline instruments here said not one pixel could
change, and the VOID captures (Line_0064.*, Line_FFFFFFFF -- the device draws
them at 1.0) each moved 1,402 -> 1,401 under a must_not_move glob.

The cause is now understood and fixed.  The clip planes are floor()/ceil() of
arbitrary reals, so an overhang of a hundredth of a pixel still crosses one:
the clip was BITING on 3 to 20 of each capture's 57 edges down to w = 0.625,
cutting slivers far too shallow to contain a pixel centre.  A float64
rasterisation at exact centres calls that inert, correctly.  Silicon computes
the cut fraction f = da / (da - db) in float32 over a sliver-sized numerator
and snaps every emitted vertex to 1/256 of a pixel, so a corner that used to
be emitted verbatim comes back re-quantised -- which is what those eight
captures measured.

cap_clip() now returns its input untouched when the polygon violates a plane
by less than HALF A PIXEL.  That threshold is derived, not tuned: the planes
land on whole pixel INDICES, this renderer rasterises one sample per pixel at
the pixel CENTRE (every rasterizationSamples under pgraph/vk/ is
VK_SAMPLE_COUNT_1_BIT, and nothing in pgraph/gl/ enables multisampling), so
the nearest sample to a bound is half a pixel away and a shallower cut
provably removes none.  It also predicts, from the geometry alone, the
model's own first moving capture: the deepest sliver per capture crosses
0.5 px between w = 16 (0.468) and w = 24 (0.704), and Line_0024.0 is where
--shader first moves.

LEG C1 -- THE CAP LEG, read by hand off arm B, not in `expect`.

  docs/testing/line_cap_phase.py --vs-goldens <armB captures>

PREDICTED: at most 600 mismatched px over the 48 non-void Line_* captures.
ARM A: ~908 px (extent fix, no cap clip).  FAILS IF: above 600 px.
The bound holds under either modelling of the tie -- 21 px and 544 px both
clear it -- while arm A's 908 px does not, so the leg separates "the cap clip
is drawn and works" from "nothing happened", which is the only distinction
the offline model is entitled to make given the tie uncertainty.  It is a
whole-capture total over 48 captures and has no capture name, which is why it
lives here and not in a field request.sh would refuse.

LEG C2 -- THE DEADBAND'S OWN CLAIM, and the machine-read leg of this file.
Below the deadband's reach emit_line() emits master's four corners, in
master's order, with master's values: the widened path's only new geometry is
the cut vertex, and where the clip does not bite there is none.  So every
capture the device draws narrower than w = 24 must be BIT-IDENTICAL between
the arms, not merely no worse.  That is the must_not_move list:

  Line_width/Line_0000.*, Line_0001.*, Line_000[3-9].0, Line_001[0-6].0
      every capture below w = 24, where the deadband says the emitted
      geometry is master's own.  Eight of these were WORSE on the failing arm
      and Line_0001.0, Line_0008.0, Line_0011.0, Line_0015.0, Line_0016.0
      were better; both directions are now predicted to be zero.
  Line_width/Line_0064.*, Line_width/Line_FFFFFFFF
      VOID: the width register holds nine bits of eighths, 64.0 does not fit,
      hardware drew all nine at 1.0 and the device draws them at 1.0 too.
      Each moved 1,402 -> 1,401 on the failing arm.  Narrow, so the deadband
      covers them.
  Line_width/Fill_*
      fill mode; with widen_lines false the generator emits the byte-identical
      shader it emitted before, so a line change must not touch them.
      Fill_0032.0 moved 26,721 -> 26,715 on the failing arm and nothing in
      this branch's diff can reach it.  The glob stays: with two runs per arm
      the judge can tell a real movement from device nondeterminism, and
      dropping a tripwire that fired is how a gate stops being one.
  Blend_tests/*
      the geometry push-constant range is declared on EVERY graphics pipeline,
      whether or not it has a geometry shader, so a mistake there shows up on
      a suite that draws no wide lines at all.

FAILS IF: any of them moves.  `line_cap_phase.py --quantise` is the offline
form of this leg -- the same polygon with every vertex snapped to the 1/256
grid, scored against the unclipped parallelogram, with the deadband-at-zero
mutant inside the check -- and it reads 0 quantised px moved after, against 4
px on 4 captures before, three of which are on the device's own mover list.
It reproduces the CLASS and under-counts the SIZE (4 px offline against 13
captures moved on the device), because it models neither float32 cut
arithmetic nor the rasteriser's fill rule.  It is a tripwire, not a predictor.

LEG C3 -- WHAT IS NOT PREDICTED AT THE WIDE END, and why `worse: 0` is gone.
Two of the ten worse captures were at w >= 63: Line_0063.0 (+2) and
Line_0063.1 (+6), where the clip legitimately bites and --quantise reports the
same numbers with the deadband as without.  Those two are the tie-bias
residual this derivation has declined to chase from its first registration
(the bias is pinned by the extent legs and by subPixelPrecisionBits; trading
them away to win coverage pixels would be a bad trade made blind).  So
expect_counts: {"worse": 0} is RETIRED as the machine leg: it is a global
tally that binds the residual as tightly as it binds the defect, and after
this remediation I do not believe it.  What I do believe, stated before the
arm: at most those two captures are worse, each by no more than the +2 and +6
already measured.  A THIRD worse capture anywhere, or either of those two
worse by more, falsifies this file -- read it off the verdict's mover table.
C2 above is what replaces it in machine-read form, and it is strictly stronger
where this remediation acts: must not move at all, rather than must not worsen.

RUNS PER ARM IS 2, deliberately.  The failing arm was one run per side, so its
"noise 0" was one run per arm with nothing to estimate from rather than a
measured zero, and ab_compare's byte-identity half of must_not_move only fails
on multi-run evidence (a single-run byte difference has the same signature as
device nondeterminism).  Both of those matter to C2, which is an assertion
about bytes.

WHY BOTH REFS MOVED.  Registered after the pass-2 audit's remediation and
after master was merged forward, in that order, so nothing rebases under it.
a_ref is master's own tip so that the two arms differ by this branch and
nothing else; b_ref names the deadbanded shader.

WHAT I DO NOT PREDICT.  The COLOUR at an overlap -- #13's separate priority
rule and 76.3% of the issue's residual; this is a coverage measurement.  The
~544 px tie-bias residual.  The GL renderer, which is untouched here (the
widened path is opts.vulkan only).  Any total for Point size, Point params,
Swath width, Smoothing control, Stipple tests or 2D Lines.
